subject: Post-demo: performance concordance & acceptance gates
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@cogenthealth.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@riverside.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarifications after today’s demo

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the walkthrough — the streaming demo answered a lot of our questions. A couple of follow-ups from our side to help our SREs and procurement team align internally:

- Latency: during the session we saw token streaming start within ~80ms for short prompts, but there were occasional p95 spikes to ~1.1s on longer, 600-token prompts. Can you confirm which model variant and batching settings you used for the demo?

- Throughput/concurrency: we want to validate sustained 120 concurrent active streams (each user sending ~1 req/minute) with 95th percentile end-to-end latency under 700ms. Is that within the standard Dedicated profile or will we need a custom pool?

- Streaming semantics: how does Redwood handle partial-response fallback if the KV cache misses on a cold connection? We need an explicit acceptance test that covers mid-stream recovery.

If you can send a short checklist of acceptance gates and any telemetry/samples you recorded during the run, that would help us convert this into a pilot scope.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Cogent Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@cogenthealth.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications after today’s demo — SLO checklist attached

Hi Elena — great to hear the demo was useful. Below is a concise recap of what we ran and a proposed set of acceptance gates you can present to your SRE and procurement teams. Attaching raw telemetry and a formatted checklist (see attachments).

What we ran (demo environment)
- Model: open-llama-70B-quant (v1.3) pinned for deterministic kernels
- Serving config: batch size auto (continuous batching), KV cache enabled, streaming enabled with chunked responses at 128-token boundaries
- Hardware: Dedicated n1-gpu pool (A100 equivalent) — single-region (us-west)
- Observed: median token streaming start ~78ms; p95 per-token start 420ms on short prompts; end-to-end p95 for 600-token prompts peaked at ~1.12s during a synthetic load spike we induced to test autoscaling hysteresis

Proposed acceptance gates (SLO checklist) — pass/fail criteria we can run in your staging cluster:
1) Latency by prompt length
   - Short prompts (<=64 tokens): p95 end-to-end <= 350ms
   - Medium prompts (65–256 tokens): p95 end-to-end <= 550ms
   - Long prompts (257–600 tokens): p95 end-to-end <= 900ms
2) Throughput/concurrency
   - Sustained 120 concurrent active streams (1 req/min/user): p95 end-to-end <= 700ms; error rate <0.5% over 30 minutes
   - Burst tolerance: 300 concurrent streams for 2 minutes with <2% error and graceful degradation to lower-throughput model variant
3) Streaming correctness and recovery
   - Partial-response continuity: on simulated KV miss, mid-stream recovery must not produce duplicated tokens more than 0.1% of streams
   - Client reconnection: reconnection within 3s retains session token and resumes stream without beginning from start in >95% of cases
4) Resource stability
   - GPU memory stability: no OOMs under test load; KV cache hit ratio >= 88% after a 60-minute warmup

Telemetry and evidence we attached
- demo-telemetry-20280711.csv — raw traces from the demo including token start times, model variant tags, and error codes
- slo-checklist-cogent-health.xlsx — formatted acceptance gates (above) with test harness steps and expected pass/fail metrics

Next steps (proposed map)
- We propose a two-week verification run in your staging environment: week 1 — baseline runs + configuration tuning; week 2 — full acceptance gates and two 30-minute soak windows.
- Proposed owners: Redwood (Sergio) to provide test harness and run scripts; Cogent SRE (Elena) to execute in staging and provide access to infra metrics.

Let me know if these gates align with your internal bar and we’ll book a kick-off to get instrumentation access.

Attachment: demo-telemetry-20280711.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)
Attachment: slo-checklist-cogent-health.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Sergio — quick note from ops: the burst tolerance line (300 concurrent for 2 minutes) is functionally handled by our autoscaler if they use Dedicated with 20% burst headroom. We should propose explicit cost delta for that headroom in the MAP so procurement can sign off. Also, can we add an explicit 99th percentile cap for short prompts? Elena's team might want p99 <= 600ms for short prompts in prod — let's flag that as optional but call it out.

I'll draft the MAP cost delta and add an optional p99 row in the spreadsheet.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- For the streaming recovery tests, can Redwood provide a simple harness (script + docker image) that we can run in our staging to simulate KV misses and reconnections? If so, we can schedule the two-week verification for the week of July 24.
- Security: attached is a short vendor QA checklist; please confirm if any of the questions require a Redwood Private deployment (we'd prefer Hosted/Dedicated if possible).

Attachment: cogent-security-qa.pdf (PDF, 230KB)
